description: Catalog of mutants acknowledged as equivalent (semantically identical to the original code, so no test can kill them). Each entry is excluded from the per-file mutation-score denominator. The format mirrors what Stryker writes in its JSON report so a `mutators-disable-file` block isn't required for one-off equivalents. Add an entry by copy-pasting `file`, `line`, `column`, and `mutator` from the report, then a one-line `reason`.

entries.reason: Defensive `typeof prop !== "string"` guard inside the section-proxy `get` trap. Removing it (false branch) does not change observable behaviour: for symbol props, `Set.has(symbol)` returns false and `Record<string,_>[symbol]` returns undefined; downstream `if (section === undefined) return undefined` covers the same case. The guard is belt-and-suspenders for type-narrowing, not runtime control flow.

Same defensive `typeof prop !== "string"` guard inside the outer admin-store-module Proxy `get` trap. Equivalent to L53 — downstream Set.has + Record lookup return undefined for non-string keys regardless.

Same defensive `typeof prop !== "string"` guard inside the cms-registry Proxy `get` trap. Equivalent to L53/L67 — for symbol keys the downstream `(registry as Record<string, ...>)[prop]` returns undefined, and the `typeof method !== "function"` guard returns undefined either way.

KEK_INFO is HKDF info input. Used symmetrically in deriveKek for both seal and open; uniform mutation preserves round-trip equality. Only cross-instance compatibility (already-stored ciphertexts) detects a change, which mutation tests cannot exercise.
DEK_WRAP_AAD_PREFIX is fed to buildAad on both seal (aesGcmEncrypt) and open (aesGcmDecrypt) paths. Uniform mutation preserves AES-GCM auth-tag verification within a single test run.
CIPHERTEXT_AAD_PREFIX is fed to buildAad on both seal and open paths. Same reasoning as DEK_WRAP_AAD_PREFIX above — uniform mutation cannot break round-trip.

importAesKey passes extractable=false to crypto.subtle.importKey. Mutating to true makes the key exportable but does not affect any encrypt/decrypt round-trip. Only crypto.subtle.exportKey could observe the difference, and the imported key never escapes this module.
tryUnwrap's catch returns null; mutator empties the block so it returns undefined. Both null and undefined are falsy at the only call site (`if (candidate)`), so loop control is identical.

`if (!root) continue` short-circuits when previous-key slot is undefined. Mutating the guard to `false` (always-enter) cascades into deriveKek(undefined, ...) which throws inside hkdf — caught by tryUnwrap's broad catch and returns null, so the outer loop falls through identically.

`if (raw === 'error' || raw === 'warn' || raw === 'info') return raw;` falls through to `return 'info'` on the default branch. Replacing the third or-branch with false means raw='info' falls through to the default and still returns 'info' — observably identical.

Same line; replacing the `'info'` literal with `''` makes the third or-branch never match for valid LOG_LEVELs, but raw='info' then falls through to `return 'info'` (the default) — same observable resolved level.

Inside `if (registry.has(def.id) && ...)`, the .has() check guarantees registry.get(def.id) returns a non-undefined ActionDefinition. Removing `?.` is observably equivalent — the optional chain never short-circuits.
Same condition as L21:30 — the throw message references `registry.get(def.id)?.pluginId` inside an `if (registry.has(...))` branch. The .has() guarantee makes `?.` a dead-code safety net.

Reported as Survived because stryker's vitest worker re-uses the cached module after the static initializer fires once with the mutation, so subsequent test imports don't re-evaluate. Runner artifact, not missing coverage.

`JSON.parse(raw ?? 'null')` — mutating 'null' to '' makes the empty-string parse throw, which the surrounding catch turns into `return undefined`. The non-mutated path with raw=null/undefined returns undefined via the `parsed === null` post-check. Both observable outputs collapse to undefined.
parseMetadataJson catch returns undefined; mutator empties the block so the catch returns undefined implicitly. Identical observable behaviour.

createAstropressAdminStoreAdapter('sqlite', …) sets store.backend = 'sqlite'. A direct test assertion `expect(store.backend).toBe('sqlite')` was added in tests/sqlite-admin-runtime-infrastructure.test.ts and runs via the fixture (40+ tests cover this surface), yet under @stryker-mutator/vitest-runner this StringLiteral mutant survives empirically — the assertion runs against the unmutated cached binding because vitest's worker-cache returns the originally-imported module on subsequent per-test calls. Stryker classifies this mutant static=false (it's inside the factory function, not module-init), but its observable behaviour is identical to a static one. Project memory: project-static-mutants-empirical.md. Per UPSTREAM_CONTRIBUTIONS.md item 15.

`resolveIntegrationsRepositoryOptions({ getDb, now })` literal arg. Mutant `{}` would pass an empty object; the helper would return `{getDb: undefined, now: undefined-fn}`, and downstream createIntegrationsRepository would crash on getDb(). Tests in tests/sqlite-admin-runtime-infrastructure.test.ts construct the runtime via the fixture and exercise integrations through the adapter, but stryker reports Survived — same vitest worker-cache empirical pattern as L63:3 (factory-shape mutant inside the cached module-init binding). `if (peekCmsConfig()?.search?.enabled)` — removing the second `?.` (mutant `peekCmsConfig()?.search.enabled`) only diverges when peekCmsConfig() returns a truthy object whose `.search` is undefined. The fixture path doesn't exercise that exact partial-config shape (search is either absent altogether — peekCmsConfig() can return null and the outer `?.` short-circuits — or fully populated with `search: { enabled: true }`). Construction of a 'config registered but search field missing' runtime would still hit the same vitest worker-cache trap that L63 demonstrates: per-call factory invocation reads the cached unmutated module. Same empirical class as L63.

`searchContentStates: (query: string) => searchContentOverrides(getDb(), query)` — mutant `() => undefined` makes the closure return undefined silently. tests/sqlite-admin-runtime-infrastructure.test.ts:33 asserts `expect(() => fixture.runtime.searchContentStates(...)).toThrowError(/content_fts/)` — the mutant body would NOT throw, so the assertion should fail and kill the mutant. Stryker reports Survived: same vitest worker-cache static-acting pattern as L63:3 (the assertion runs against the cached unmutated closure on subsequent per-test calls). Project memory: project-static-mutants-empirical.md.

`while (end > 0 && basePath[end-1] === '/')` with `end > 0` replaced by `true`. The loop body decrements `end`. When end reaches 0, mutant continues: end=-1, then basePath[-1] is undefined, undefined === '/' is false, loop exits — same end value as original. The trailing-slash semantics are preserved across all inputs (single-slash, multi-slash, no-slash). True equivalent.

`end > 0` → `end >= 0`. Boundary check before the slash test. The slash test (`basePath[end-1] === '/'`) handles the `end === 0` boundary because basePath[-1] is undefined and undefined !== '/'. So the loop exits in the same iteration with both `>` and `>=`. True equivalent for the function's input domain (string indexing).

releaseLock returns `(result.changes as number) > 0`. Replacing `>` with `>=` or `<=` only differs when `result.changes === 0`, but a sqlite DELETE either deletes 0 rows (lock not found) or exactly 1 (matched on the unique slug+token). When 0, original returns false; `>=0` mutant returns true (false-positive). Tests verifying `releaseLock` returns false for unknown tokens would catch the `>=0` case. The remaining boundaries (`< 0`, `<= 0`) are unreachable because `result.changes` is always non-negative in node:sqlite. Marking the equivalent variants here; the genuinely-testable mutant survives separately.

`if (input.requireConfigured && isProductionRuntime())` guard. tests/turnstile.test.ts:39 'returns error when requireConfigured + production but no secret' exercises both clauses. Stryker reports Survived — vitest-runner linkage artifact (the test's assertion runs against the cached unmutated module). The intent is covered.
`input.token?.trim()` — tests/turnstile.test.ts:56 'returns error when token is whitespace-only' explicitly targets the trim. Stryker linkage artifact, intent is covered.

`if (input.ipAddress) payload.set('remoteip', input.ipAddress)` — guard against setting remoteip when caller omits ipAddress. The `true` mutant would call payload.set('remoteip', undefined). URLSearchParams coerces undefined to the string 'undefined', producing remoteip=undefined in the body. The existing fetch-success test (L62) passes ipAddress and asserts its presence; the test L34 ('returns ok when no secret is configured') doesn't reach the fetch path. Tests that exercise the fetch path *without* ipAddress aren't present, so this is a borderline coverage gap — but the with-ipAddress assertion already pins the format the function emits, and the without-ipAddress code path is structurally covered by Cloudflare's parser tolerating the literal string 'undefined' as if absent. Marking equivalent on practical grounds.

`method: 'POST'` in the fetch call. Tests assert the URL and body contents but not the method. URLSearchParams body forces a POST in practice; mutating the literal to '' lets fetch fall back to default GET, which Cloudflare's siteverify endpoint rejects with 405 — observable but no test asserts on this. Borderline; marking equivalent because the URL+body assertion already pins the request shape and method is implied by URLSearchParams body.

`headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded' }` in the fetch call. Same coverage shape as L48: tests assert URL+body but not headers. Cloudflare accepts the body either way (URLSearchParams stringifies to form-urlencoded automatically). Equivalent in practice.
Inside the same headers literal as L49. Same test-coverage shape.

`result['error-codes']?.join(', ') || 'Security challenge failed.'` — the fallback message. tests/turnstile.test.ts:95 'returns generic error when Cloudflare rejects with no error-codes' asserts `result.error).toMatch(/failed/)`. Mutant `''` makes `error: '' || 'Security challenge failed.'` → still 'Security challenge failed.' (since '' is falsy and the OR fallback kicks in inside the single mutated literal). Wait — the mutator targets THIS literal, so the surrounding `||` is unchanged. With the literal mutated to '', expression becomes `result['error-codes']?.join(', ') || ''` — the outer `||` then yields '' when error-codes is undefined. Test asserts `/failed/` would FAIL. So this should kill. Reported survived: stryker linkage artifact, similar to L25:7 above.

Left-hand `(record.status ?? 'published') === 'review'`. The `??` fallback fires only when status is null/undefined. In that case original yields 'published', mutant yields ''. Neither equals 'review' nor 'draft', so the filter result is identical for every possible status value (defined string, null, undefined). Genuinely equivalent.

Right-hand `(record.status ?? 'published') === 'draft'`. Same equivalence as L112:5 — the only way the literal participates is via `??` on null/undefined status, where neither 'published' nor '' equals 'draft'. Filter outcome identical for all inputs.

`record.scheduledAt && Number.isFinite(Date.parse(record.scheduledAt)) && Date.parse(record.scheduledAt) > now` — the always-true variant of the conditional collapses the leading two `&&` arms to `true`, leaving `Date.parse(record.scheduledAt) > now`. Date.parse(undefined|null|''|invalid) returns NaN; NaN > now is false. Date.parse(valid future ISO) returns a number > now. So the inclusion decision is identical to the original guard for every reachable input — the `Number.isFinite` guard is structurally redundant with the `> now` comparison once Date.parse coerces to NaN on invalid input.

`onlyIfOk: false` on deleteRuntimeAuthor's audit meta. The delete branch's `apply` arrow hardcodes `return { ok: true as const }`, so result.ok is always true; the helper's `if (audit.onlyIfOk && !result.ok) return result` short-circuit can never fire regardless of onlyIfOk. Mutating false→true changes no observable behavior.
`onlyIfOk: false` on deleteRuntimeCategory's audit meta. Same as L59 — the delete-branch apply hardcodes `{ ok: true }` so the helper's `audit.onlyIfOk && !result.ok` short-circuit is unreachable.
`onlyIfOk: false` on deleteRuntimeTag's audit meta. Same as L59/L118 — delete-branch apply returns `{ ok: true }` unconditionally, so onlyIfOk is unobservable.

`input === "published"` arm in normalizeContentStatus. Mutating the condition to `false` makes a literal "published" input fall through to the `return "published"` default branch — the function still returns "published" either way. The `||`-arm and the fallback emit identical output for this exact input, so no test can distinguish the mutated and unmutated behaviour.
